ajay: Heads-up — since yesterday's runtime tweak (auto-kernel-sel v2) we've seen a spike in GPU OOMs on prod-03 during mixed chat workloads. Saw 14 OOMs in 2h starting ~07:12 UTC. :eyes:

maria: Ugh. Any correlation with cache stats or batch sizes?

ajay: Yes. Quick summary from the perf dashboard: overall latency unchanged, but prefix/KV cache effective hit-rate dropped from ~83% -> ~41% for client-heavy sessions matching the debug promptset. Also GPU free memory fragmentation increased. Suspect two things: the new kernel selection path changes key ordering and an internal allocator bug that prevents reuse of freed KV slabs.

lucas: Can you paste the cache dump and the nsys snippet?

ajay: Pasted below. It's terse — i pulled the metrics from /internal/metrics on prod-03 around 07:20.

```
# /internal/metrics snapshot
kv_cache.total_entries: 124512
kv_cache.effective_hits: 51321
kv_cache.requests: 123987
kv_cache.avg_entry_size_bytes: 8192
kv_cache.free_slabs: 8
kv_cache.allocated_slabs: 192
kv_cache.evictions: 87
kv_cache.eviction_policy: lru
kv_cache.key_scheme: prefix+sessionid
```

nsys region: short:
```
GPU free (MB): before 4096 -> after 1200
alloc/reclaim patterns: many small frees then big allocs -> fragmentation
nvtx markers: kv_alloc, kv_free, kernel_launch
```

maria: That key_scheme stands out — prefix+sessionid will blow up key cardinality if sessionid is ephemeral. Why did we change keying?

ajay: It was part of a fix to avoid cross-session prefix collisions during canary. But evidently session IDs were appended to the key even for identical prefixes which prevented hits across requests and caused cache bloat. The kernel selection path then chose a different layout for the in-memory KV index (reorders buckets) which made fragmentation worse when slabs couldn't be reused because we were holding stale per-session refs.

taylor: So two failure modes: cache miss storm (higher backend work -> higher alloc pressure) + fragmentation in slab allocator (can't satisfy large contiguous KV allocations) -> OOM. Right?

ajay: Exactly. Also noticed LRU had been semi-disabled in the same deploy by a TTL flag flip (devs turned TTL to 0 for debugging and forgot to re-enable). So eviction didn't reclaim as expected. :facepalm:

lucas: Nice catch. Do we have a repro locally? If we can reproduce, we can test fixes: (1) revert keying to stable-prefix-only, (2) re-enable TTL/eviction in canary window, (3) compact/free-list coalescing in allocator, (4) warmup prefetch for top-N prefixes on model switch, (5) temporary cap on per-session cache entries.

ajay: I made a small local repro script that simulates the problematic workload (many short sessions, identical prompts but unique session IDs). It recreates the hit-rate drop and fragmentation pattern. I'll push it to the perf repo. Patch plan below.

```
# repro outline (python)
for i in range(10000):
  sid = uuid4()
  client.send(prefix + sid)
  # short tail requests, expect identical prefix hits but get misses
```

maria: Proposed fixes + risk assessment?

ajay: Short-term rollback is safe: revert key change AND flip TTL back to 24h (or previous setting). That should restore hit-rate and let LRU evict. Medium-term: allocator improvements are slightly invasive but low-risk if feature-flagged: coalesce adjacent free slabs and add a background compaction pass during low-load windows. Also add a metric "kv_cache_effective_hit_rate_v2" that ignores session-scoped keys so we can alert on anomalous splits.

lucas: Can we add a heuristic to the kernel selector to avoid reordering index buckets on hot paths? If kernel selection churns the internal layout, it amplifies fragmentation. Maybe pin the kernel for N minutes after a model/variant rollout.

ajay: Good idea — I'll add a conservative pin for 10 minutes post-deploy. That buys stability while we monitor.

runtime-bot: Deploy job #5243 started (canary -> prod-03) by ajay. Expect ~15m rollout.

maria: Who owns the allocator patch? I can take the background compaction work but need pointers to the slab layout code.

ajay: assigning to maria for allocator compaction. I'll handle keying rollback and TTL flip. Lucas will add the kernel-pin heuristic. Taylor can write the test harness and add an alert rule: trigger if kv_cache_effective_hit_rate drops >30% vs baseline for 10m AND GPU free fragmentation metric > 30%.

taylor: adding alert to runbook. Also suggest runbook step: if hit-rate low -> check key scheme and TTL flags; if fragmentation high -> live compact (if enabled) or restart runtime on that host to reclaim contiguous memory. Restart is last resort.

lucas: One more note — batching heuristics: during the miss storm we saw tiny batches (N=1) increasing kernel-launch overhead. Add a temporary heuristic to coalesce requests with identical prefixes within 2ms window to amortize kernel cost while cache warms. Should be behind flag.

ajay: Timeline: rollback + TTL flip now, canary deploy in 15m. Allocator patch + kernel-pin next sprint. I'll attach the perf repro and the minimal metrics dashboard in the PR.

maria: Thanks. I'll prototype compaction and run it in staging with load script.

runtime-bot: Deploy job #5243 finished: canary passed on prod-03. Monitoring window open for 30m.

ajay: Early numbers (10m after rollback): effective hit-rate back to ~79%, OOMs stopped, fragmentation metric falling. We'll keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:

maria: Nice work team. Follow-ups: PRs for (1) keying revert, (2) TTL config sanity check, (3) allocator compaction RFC. I'll open RFC today.

taylor: I'll add the alert and update runbook steps.

ajay: Closing loop: patch links and repro repo -> https://git.internal/redwood/perf/repro/kv-frag-1758004321

lucas: Good postmortem. Add a short note in incidents channel once RFC lands.

ajay: Will do.
